description: The bar chart, titled “Factual Errors,” illustrates the number of factual errors made by three different question-answering (QA) systems — NoR QA (orange with diagonal stripes), OneR QA (red with polka dots), and IRCoT QA (blue with diagonal crosshatch) — across four benchmark datasets: HotpotQA, 2WikiMQA, MuSiQue, and IIRC. The vertical y-axis represents the count of factual errors, ranging from 0 to 40 in increments of 5. For HotpotQA, NoR QA committed 15 errors, OneR QA 10, and IRCoT QA 5. On 2WikiMQA, errors were 29 (NoR QA), 23 (OneR QA), and 14 (IRCoT QA). For MuSiQue, the values were 28 (NoR QA), 27 (OneR QA), and 23 (IRCoT QA). Finally, on IIRC, the systems recorded 15 (NoR QA), 14 (OneR QA), and 11 (IRCoT QA) errors respectively. Across all datasets, IRCoT QA consistently exhibits the lowest number of factual errors, suggesting improved accuracy through interleaving retrieval with chain-of-thought reasoning, as proposed in the paper. The bars are grouped by dataset along the horizontal axis, with each group containing three adjacent bars corresponding to the three QA methods, and error counts are explicitly labeled atop each bar.
